title: Deref Abuse for Code Reuse (Inheritance Tax)
pattern: Abusing Rust's `Deref` trait on a custom struct solely to inherit or reuse helper methods from an inner struct, exposing the entire target API to public callers.
why_bad: It violates the contract of `Deref` (which is intended strictly for smart pointers). It leaks the inner utility API to the public interface of the outer struct, creating a confusing hybrid and breaking clean abstraction barriers.
detection: An implementation of `Deref` where the outer type is not a conceptual smart pointer (like `Rc`, `Box`, `Arc`) or wrapper, but rather a standard domain/business struct.
counterexample: Conceptual smart pointers or container types where transparent forwarding is mathematically logical.
fix: Use explicit delegation or pass the inner helper struct as an argument instead of abusing automatic dereferencing.
source: Andrew Hunt & David Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer* (2019), Topic 34 ("Inheritance Tax" / delegation alternatives); Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 6.
